submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent at 1.99e-5 A. I searched the Bi-vanadate (BiVO4-like) region, the known strong photoanode family in this system. Photocurrent rose steadily as Bi fell and V rose: index 49 gave 1.81e-6 A, index 63 gave 1.60e-5 A and index 44 gave 1.99e-5 A. Model results mattered little. The only phase I could identify, CuO (on the hull by MACE, near-zero gap by MEGNet), supports avoiding Cu-rich compositions.

rejected.reason: Likely to phase-separate toward narrow-gap CuO, which makes a poor photoanode. Not measured.
May continue the upward trend, but the merit budget was used up. Not measured.

consultations.verdict: Uninformative: the only valid receipt is a MEGNet HSE gap of 0.316 eV for mp-704645, a phase whose formula I couldn't see because the phase list was too large to read. That gap is too small for a good photoanode, but it doesn't bear on index 49. I'm choosing 49 on domain grounds: at Bi 0.40 / V 0.43 it is the candidate closest to 1:1 Bi:V, i.e. to BiVO4, the best-known photoanode in this system and one that absorbs at 3.2 eV.

Weakly supports steering away from Cu-rich regions. MACE puts mp-704645, which is CuO, on the hull (0.001 eV/atom), and MEGNet gives it a gap of only 0.32 eV. So the Cu-rich compositions probably phase-separate toward narrow-gap CuO, which is a poor photoanode. I'm choosing index 63 (Bi 0.36 / V 0.46 / Cu 0.18). It stays near the BiVO4-like region, where index 49 gave 1.81e-6 A, and sits between 49 and the GP's second pick, 44.

Mildly against Cu-rich points and uninformative for index 44. MEGNet's PBE gap for CuO (mp-704645) is about 0.04 eV, which confirms CuO-rich regions are poor for 3.2 eV photoanode operation. I'm choosing 44 on measured data: photocurrent rose about 9x from index 49 to 63 as Bi fell and V rose. Index 44 (Bi 0.33 / Cu 0.20 / V 0.47) is the next step along that direction and stays in the Bi-vanadate region.
